newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian truckers settle key demand with gov't.
newsitem.headline: Colombian truckers settle key demand with gov't.

text.p: Striking Colombian truckers settled a key demand with the government early Friday, clearing the way for a possible quick end to the crippling six-day-old work stoppage, a government official said.
Jose Noe Rios, Colombia's deputy Labor Minister and chief negotiator with the truckers, said a final issued remained unresolved, however.
"We've settled the issue of freights," Rios told Radionet news program, referring to the strikers' chief demand that the government establish minimum cargo rates for highway freight.
The agreement, which Rios did not elaborate on, came after more than 19 hours of non-stop talks at the Transportation Ministry in central Bogota.

Rios said the strike had not yet been lifted, however, and stressed that union officials were now insisting that the government lift tonnage limits on some vehicles to allow them to haul larger cargo loads.

"This is a request that the government has said is not negotiable," Rios said, adding that the authorities had ruled out any change in weight limits because of potential damage to the country's already battered highway infrastructure.
"They (the truckers) say this is a fundamental point for them, but the government insists it is not open to negotiation," Rios said.

Colombian Truck Drivers' Association represents about 80 percent of Colombian truckers. It began its strike, which was declared illegal as of midnight Thursday, to protest the failure of government and private transportation officials to fulfill terms of a pact ending an 11-day strike last October.
